correctness.rationale: The transform \(T=-\log F_R(X)\) has exact Lomax survival \([\beta/(\beta+t)]^\alpha\). The inverse-map Jacobian is exact and has \(\log J(t)=-t/2+O(1)\) at infinity and only logarithmic growth near zero. Since the Lomax density is bounded at zero, the positive log-Jacobian part is integrable; the negative tail is integrable exactly when \(\mathbb E T<\infty\), i.e. \(\alpha>1\). This proves finite entropy exactly above the threshold and \(-\infty\) below it. The checker independently reproduces the transformation, tail ratio, and explicit expectations.

value.rationale: Shannon entropy is presented as a fundamental property of the new model. The result identifies the exact parameter region where that property is a finite number, shows that the entropy is actually \(-\infty\) on the entire \(0<\alpha\le1\) region, and evaluates two expectations the source leaves numerical. This prevents invalid numerical interpretation of divergent terms and gives a reusable transformed-variable representation of the model.
